summary: Master nutrition programme design and evaluation. Learn logic models, COM-B, dietary assessment, and M&E frameworks. Enrol in this 5-day expert-led course.
lede: Nutrition intervention planning connects assessed needs with activities and measurable dietary outcomes. Designed for professionals in nutrition, public health, dietetics and health programme management, the course covers dietary assessment, logic models and behaviour-change strategy selection. Learners also practise setting nutrition indicators and planning process and outcome evaluations to assess implementation and report findings.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate-level professionals who are already working in nutrition, public health, dietetics, or health programme management and who need to strengthen their ability to design structured nutrition programmes and evaluate their impact with credible evidence.
audience: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialists embedded in nutrition
modules: Nutrition Programme Context and Needs Assessment
Programme Logic and Theory of Change
Dietary Behaviour Change: COM-B and the Behaviour Change Wheel
Nutrition Intervention Design and Implementation Planning
Nutrition Outcome Indicators and Monitoring Frameworks
Process Evaluation: Fidelity, Reach, and Implementation Quality
Reporting, Stakeholder Communication, and Programme Adaptation
prerequisites: Participants should bring a current or recent nutrition programme context — a project they manage, have managed, or are planning — to use as the basis for the applied exercises throughout the course. A laptop or tablet is required for the digital data collection and dashboard exercises. No specialist software licences are needed in advance; the course uses REDCap (free, open-source), ODK (free, open-source), and free-tier versions of data visualisation tools. Datasets and exercise templates are provided by the facilitator.
